method: The page estimates bitterness with the Tinseth utilisation model, the standard home-brewing equation. Utilisation is the product of a gravity factor, 1.65 x 0.000125^(SG - 1), which falls as the wort thickens, and a boil-time factor, (1 - e^(-0.04 t)) / 4.15, which rises with minutes and levels off. The two factors are multiplied and applied to the alpha acid mass, (alpha% / 100) x grams x 1000 x utilisation / litres of kettle volume, so one IBU is one milligram of isomerised alpha acid per litre. The page asks for the kettle volume and the average boil gravity rather than the topped-up fermenter figures, evaluates each addition independently, and shows the utilisation and alpha acid concentration behind every contribution. The model covers the boil only: a 0-minute addition contributes nothing, and whirlpool, hop-stand and dry-hop additions are not counted, so the result is a floor for heavily late-hopped beers. It assumes whole-cone hops, since pellets isomerise somewhat better, and kettle geometry, boil vigour, pH and altitude are not modelled; the figure is an estimate of measured IBU, not a measurement, and does not predict how bitter the beer tastes.
